source_first_audit.profile_reason: bounded default profile for a high-frequency adverb with one ordered-correspondence sense

coverage_axes.notes: Independent general dictionaries agree on the ordered-correspondence sense; the secondary separately gloss and historical senses are explicitly dispositioned.
The adverb category and its list-pairing placement are covered by learner and general dictionaries.
The respective + -ly formation and the related adjective respective are recorded.
The bounded inventory found no distinct specialist or legal sense for this high-frequency adverb; specialist/legal source expansion is not warranted for the one-sense draft.
General dictionary coverage and Collins regional pronunciation information support the standard register and US/UK distinction.
Learner-dictionary pronunciation and historical etymology sources cover pronunciation, formation, and related form.

facts.statement: Respectively refers to two or more people or things in the same order as they were previously mentioned.
facts.source_detail: Cambridge's headword definition centers the same-order relation to previously mentioned items.

facts.statement: The dictionary illustrates respectively after paired lists, such as Julie and Mark with the ages 17 and 19.
facts.source_detail: Cambridge supplies a paired-list age example showing first-to-first and second-to-second correspondence.

facts.statement: Respectively is an adverb meaning in the same order as people or things already mentioned.
facts.source_detail: Oxford labels the headword as an adverb and defines its ordered correspondence.
The learner dictionary provides the headword IPA in its pronunciation line.

facts.statement: Merriam-Webster defines the primary use as in the order given.
facts.source_detail: The primary adverb sense is stated as 'in the order given'.

facts.statement: Merriam-Webster also records a secondary gloss, in particular: separately.
facts.source_detail: The dictionary includes separately as a secondary gloss, which is retained for an explicit usage distinction.

facts.statement: Merriam-Webster dates the first known use of respectively to 1602.
facts.source_detail: The headword page supplies a first-known-use date; it is not needed in the learner-facing article.

facts.statement: Collins explains respectively as applying in the same order as the items just mentioned.
facts.source_detail: The COBUILD and general entries both describe the same-order pairing of two lists.

facts.statement: Collins gives US /rɪˈspɛktɪvli/ and British /rɪˈspɛktɪvlɪ/ pronunciations.
facts.source_detail: The page distinguishes the US and British pronunciation forms.

facts.statement: Collins gives the formation as respective plus the suffix -ly.
Historical records include a mid-fifteenth-century obsolete relatively sense, a 1580s archaic respectfully sense, and a 1620s sense meaning relatively to each of several singly.
facts.source_detail: The etymology entry separates earlier obsolete or archaic uses from the later each-of-several development.

facts.statement: Respectively comes from respective plus -ly; respective is related to Medieval Latin respectivus and the Latin respicere stem respect-.
facts.source_detail: The etymology entry connects the suffixal formation to the Latin look-back/consideration root.

facts.statement: Respective is the related adjective meaning considered individually or belonging to each person or thing.
facts.source_detail: The source explains the adjective base from which respectively is formed.

source_union.canonical_statement: Respectively marks a one-to-one pairing in the order in which the two lists are given.
source_union.rationale: Three independent general dictionaries converge on the article's primary ordered-correspondence definition.

source_union.canonical_statement: Some dictionaries include separately as a secondary gloss, but the article must distinguish separation from ordered pairing.
source_union.rationale: The article records the gloss while teaching the more reliable learner-facing distinction.

source_union.canonical_statement: A paired-list example demonstrates first-to-first and second-to-second correspondence.
source_union.rationale: The article's paired-value examples instantiate the same frame without copying the dictionary example.

source_union.canonical_statement: Respectively is an adverb used with matched lists.
source_union.rationale: This supports the part-of-speech label and the main grammar pattern.
The pronunciation section records the corresponding IPA.

source_union.canonical_statement: Merriam-Webster records 1602 as the first known use.
source_union.rationale: A precise first-use date is outside the scope of this learner-facing one-sense article and does not support a current usage claim.

source_union.canonical_statement: US and British pronunciation variants are distinguished.
source_union.rationale: Regional IPA is directly represented in the pronunciation section.

source_union.canonical_statement: Respectively is formed from respective plus -ly.
source_union.rationale: The word-formation and etymology sections state this formation.

source_union.canonical_statement: Earlier obsolete and archaic uses precede the later each-of-several development.
source_union.rationale: The article prioritizes the current standard adverb and does not present obsolete historical senses as live meanings.

source_union.canonical_statement: The formation is related to respective, Medieval Latin respectivus, and Latin respicere.
source_union.rationale: The current etymology paragraph presents the historical root relationship.

source_union.canonical_statement: Respective is the related adjective base.
source_union.rationale: The word-formation section contrasts the adjective with the adverb.

claim_units.statement: Respectively pairs the first item in one list with the first item in another, the second with the second, and so on.

source_supports.support_summary: Cambridge defines the same-order relation to previously mentioned people or things.
Merriam-Webster's primary gloss is in the order given.
Collins describes the same order as items just mentioned.

claim_units.statement: Respectively is not a general substitute for separately; its core use preserves ordered correspondence.

source_supports.support_summary: Merriam-Webster records separately as a secondary gloss, which the usage note qualifies.

claim_units.statement: The word can follow two paired lists of subjects and values or outcomes.

source_supports.support_summary: Cambridge's age example pairs each subject with the value in the same position.

claim_units.statement: Respectively is an adverb used to mark the paired-list relation.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford labels respectively an adverb and defines its same-order function.

claim_units.statement: The headword has the learner-dictionary pronunciation /rɪˈspektɪvli/.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford supplies the headword IPA in its pronunciation entry.

claim_units.statement: US and British pronunciations differ in the final weak vowel notation.

source_supports.support_summary: Collins lists separate US and British IPA forms for the headword.

claim_units.statement: Respectively is the adverbial form made from respective plus -ly.

source_supports.support_summary: Collins explicitly gives respective plus -ly as the origin.

claim_units.statement: The form is historically related to respective and the Latin respect-/respicere family.

source_supports.support_summary: Etymonline connects the suffixal form to respective and Latin respicere.

claim_units.statement: Respective is the related adjective base and should be distinguished from the adverb respectively.

source_supports.support_summary: The etymology source identifies respective as the related adjective base.
